To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) cell size in wild type Saccharmyces cerevisiae is distributed in a gamma distribution, and 2) mutants with altered cell size distributions are enriched for those with transcription or transcription linked gene defects

The distribution of the size of Saccharomyces cells is well fit by a gamma distribution, that the distribution of size of single gene deletion strains deviates from the gamma distribution in a way that is related to the role of genes in gene expression, and that the size distribution of Pol II mutants deviates from the expected gamma.

the size of yeast cells fit a gamma probability distribution in wild type cells and under different growth condition, that cell size distribution is influenced by the transcriptional status of a cell, and that cell size distributions of strains carrying altered activity substitutions of Rpo21p are altered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of cell size values in Saccharomyce cerevisiae,
how the size of cells varies around a characteristic distribution, rather than with how cell size is regulated.
the question of what determines the distribution of cell size values within a population of cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
perturbation of transcription and gene expression associated processes alter cell size distributions.
the size distribution of wild-type cells is a consequence of a complex network of gene expression processes.
perturbations of gene expression and associated processes alter the distribution of cell size values in Saccharomyce cerevisiae.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perturbations of transcription and gene expression associated processes alter the distribution of cell size values.
transcription and transcription related processes influence the pattern of cell size distribution in Saccharomyes cerevisiae.

the distribution of cell size values in Saccharomyes cerevisiae is a reflection of the distribution of cell sizes that are compatible with the maintenance of cell size homeostatic mechanisms, and that this distribution is perturbed in cells lacking gene products that are essential for transcription and transcription linked processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell size distributions can be used as a tool to identify genes that affect the overall pattern of cell growth and division in a population of cells.
cell size distribution is not a trivial outcome of the growth process but is the result of complex interactions between transcription, gene expression and cell growth.
the distribution of cell size values is not random, but is a property that can be perturbed by genetic defects.
